sentences.text: Orthosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms, a group of reptiles that includes modern crocodiles.
This small animal measured about 60 to 70 centimeters in length and had a body proportion similar to lizards.
Its lower jaw likely held 15 to 18 teeth of equal size and similar shape.
The skeleton possessed 24 vertebrae, with eight located in the neck region.
Orthosuchus had five digits on its limbs.
It possessed earflaps that protected its ears from water when swimming.
A small salt-secreting gland indicates it was not a marine animal.
The animal was first discovered in 1963 in the Red Beds Formation of the Qacha's Nek Province in Lesotho.
The species Orthosuchus stormbergi was named by Nash in 1968.
There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Orthosuchus.
Researchers suggest Orthosuchus may have been quadrupedal because its forelimbs were about 91% the length of its hind limbs.
Unlike modern crocodiles, Orthosuchus likely walked upright with its femur vertical to the ground rather than creeping on its belly.
Researchers suggest Orthosuchus may have hunted by slowly approaching schools of small fish and striking from the side.
It may not have been a good swimmer because its amphicoelous vertebrae lacked the tail mobility found in modern crocodiles.
Orthosuchus is classified as a reptile.
The genus belongs to the family Notochampsidae.
A 2021 revision placed Orthosuchus as the sister taxon to Notochampsa within the family Notochampsidae.
Orthosuchus lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
It is debated whether Orthosuchus belongs to the family Protosuchidae, though it shares characteristics with that group.
